pr_body:

pr_comments:
ping @climba03003 and @Eomm. 

My main doubt is the correctness of the warning messages. I would greatly appreciate any feedback you can give me.

> Please use a single deprecation warning.

I am applying all the suggestions right now. Thank you!
All the suggestion has been applied on a3094e78abe4a400fb0c6f7f2456d104d62c5d18.
Is the underlying issue actually a deprecation?

> Is the underlying issue actually a deprecation?

There is no feature to deprecate here - we are just sanitizing the input IMHO

> > Is the underlying issue actually a deprecation?
> 
> There is no feature to deprecate here - we are just sanitizing the input IMHO

Then this should not be a `FSTDEP` error. And I'm not clear why the log isn't sufficient. I think it would be tremendously more difficult to deal with a process warning than the log.
A warning is always visible and I consider this issue a security threat (a developer thinks to validate the input, but it is not)
Ready for review again, I have applied all the suggestions. Thank you!
I'm not blocking this. I haven't researched the underlying issue, but I feel like it could be solved in a better way than a process warning.

> I'm not blocking this. I haven't researched the underlying issue, but I feel like it could be solved in a better way than a process warning.

I understand your point. The underlying issue, IMHO, is an unwanted breaking change introduced on 4.15.0 (see https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4620). It could either have been reverted totally or, for instance, to apply the approach of the current PR: avoid the runtime error but highlight the security threat that the missed schema could suppose.

I'm open to working on a different approach :) Thank you for all the tremendous support you provided with my first contribution. What a welcoming Fastify community you have here 🎉 !
This pull request has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.

issue_context.title: Error: Schema for validaton is undefined
comments: @Eomm I think we should revert https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4620, and possibly undo that for v5.

I added that fix because I had undefined schemas and all was working fine. 

I tested what I was going adding into the db and I spot additional fields that was unexpected.. Then a debug session pointed me to a typo! 

I'm sure out there there are a lot of typos and developers that think to have set a validation schema.. But they are not!

I think that setting a schema as undefined is a "don't care" action. Do not add the property if you don't want the schema instead.
Instead of `full revert`, we can change to a warning for `v4` and bring it back to runtime error in `v5`.

> I added that fix because I had undefined schemas and all was working fine.

Sorry, I can't agree with you. This change was about type system and contracts, but not about security. You're trying to shift the user's responsibility on library level.

@c0sx there are two aspect at play here:
1. the unwanted breakage
2. the actual change

In Fastify, we do deprecation on the current supported line and removal in the next major. If we turned it into a warning, all your code would still work.

Overall I'm not convinced of the actual change. More specifically, `undefined` is not returned when rendering JSON, so its presence should be "neutral". I would still throw for `null`.

review_comments:
This statement will also cover situations where the schema part is `null`, for instance not it won't match the sentence given on the deprecation.

wdyt if we extend the deprecation message to make it agnostic, and just indicate that the part is missed? 🤔

Good catch! I've changed the message. See the example below. Any feedback is welcome :)
```console
[FSTDEP015] FastifyDeprecation: The params schema for GET: /:id is missed. This may indicate the schema is not well specified.
```

need a test for it - what if I have 2 routes with undefined schema? does the warning show up once?

In this case I think it should be emitted for every route

Hello @Eomm, it is emitted only once. As far as I see, [process-warning](https://github.com/fastify/process-warning) guarantees that the same warning is emitted only once.

We can't have a warning emitted for every route if we use the same warning code for all the routes. Perhaps, we could emit a warning with a dynamic code every time, but it would imply:

1. Creating the warning directly on `validations.js`.
2. The warning code would be dynamic, so we need to find a way to avoid collisions to emit still the warning for every route with "_undefined_ schema".

Please, note it is the first time I'm working on the Fastify codebase, so please, correct me if I'm wrong or if there is another simpler way than my previous thought.

Yeah, I was not 100% sure but I had a suspect

I will add this feature by the weekend so we can customize this behaviour later on
https://github.com/fastify/process-warning/blob/master/index.js

https://github.com/fastify/process-warning/pull/78 👍🏼 

You will need to add a boolean and bump the module whenever we release it please 🙏🏼
Any news for the new release of the `process-warning`? Thank you

Perfect, I've just updated the code using the new version and the new `unlimited` flag enabled. Note that the validation warning is emitted twice for GET routes, one for the method GET and another for the method HEAD.

> [FSTDEP015] FastifyDeprecation: The body schema for GET: /undefinedBody/:id is missed. This may indicate the schema is not well specified.
[FSTDEP015] FastifyDeprecation: The body schema for HEAD: /undefinedBody/:id is missed. This may indicate the schema is not well specified.
